input.rationale: Final source-grounded entry for the read-path family, because the run's budget expires at the end of this turn and this is a code-established mechanism rather than a measurement: the periodic heartbeat carries only the most recently admitted pending request context, while each admission triggers its own broadcast and acknowledgments are tracked per context. That distinction is exactly what a reviewer needs when weighing the earlier coalescing and starvation findings, so it is recorded with its sources and no execution or interpretation is claimed.

knowledge.statement: The leader's periodic heartbeat path attaches the read-only context of only the most recently admitted pending request: bcastHeartbeat takes readOnly.lastPendingRequestCtx(), which returns the rctx of the last entry in readIndexQueue and an empty value when the queue is empty, and passes it to bcastHeartbeatWithCtx (raft.go:722-730 with read_only.go:114-121). Each admission instead triggers its own broadcast carrying that request's rctx through sendMsgReadIndexResponse, and acknowledgments are tracked per context bytes by readOnly.recvAck, with readOnly.advance dequeuing the statuses up to the acknowledged context (raft.go:2142-2157, read_only.go:68-112). So a periodic heartbeat refreshes only the latest pending request, every pending request has already had its own admission-time broadcast, and no context is attached when nothing is pending.
knowledge.conditions: The node is StateLeader with ReadOnlySafe; read requests are admitted through MsgReadIndex so that statuses exist in readOnly, and the heartbeat timer fires while the queue is either empty or non-empty.

knowledge.statement: In StateLeader with the ReadOnlySafe option, when a MsgReadIndex arrives whose Entries[0].Data equals the rctx of a request that is already recorded in readOnly.pendingReadIndex, readOnly.addRequest returns early without storing the new request message, and sendMsgReadIndexResponse still attaches a heartbeat with that rctx (bcastHeartbeatWithCtx) and re-acknowledges the local node; the readIndexQueue and pendingReadIndex therefore keep exactly one status for the two admissions, and no second request message is retained.
knowledge.conditions: Node is in StateLeader, ReadOnlyOption is ReadOnlySafe (the default), the leader has committed an entry in its current term so stepLeader calls sendMsgReadIndexResponse directly, the earlier request with the equal rctx is still pending (not yet advanced), and no reset/become* has occurred between the two admissions.

knowledge.statement: On the acknowledging heartbeat, stepLeader asks readOnly.advance for the statuses up to the acknowledged ctx and then answers each returned status through responseToReadIndexReq(rs.req, rs.index): a status whose stored request came from a remote peer produces one MsgReadIndexResp addressed to that stored request's From, and a status whose stored request came from the leader itself appends one local ReadState. Only the request message of the first admission with a given rctx is stored, so admissions that were discarded by addRequest produce no read index answer of either kind.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlySafe with a quorum of heartbeat acknowledgments carrying the ctx, leader state unchanged between admission and acknowledgment, and the discarded admission having used the same rctx bytes as the stored one.

knowledge.statement: In the retained execution of the fixed experiment (three-voter cluster {1,2,3} in one process, node 1 leader in term 1 with a committed entry in its term, ReadOnlySafe, fault-free ordered delivery), the ReadIndex request admitted first (parsed event 1, requester 2, rctx 'assurance-dup-rctx') received one MsgReadIndexResp and one ReadState, while the equal-rctx request admitted second (event 2, requester 3) received no MsgReadIndexResp and no ReadState (event 13: responded=false, responses=0, requester_read_states=0) over the following eight leader heartbeat rounds (events 4-11: leader_state=StateLeader, pending=0, undelivered=0, cumulative responses_to_3=0) whose acknowledgments were produced by the real follower state machines. With two different rctxes both requesters were answered (events 15-18), and with a single requester retrying its own rctx that requester was answered (events 20-21).

knowledge.statement: In stepLeader, a MsgReadIndex whose sender passes the leader checks is answered immediately through sendMsgReadIndexResponse only when the leader has committed an entry in its current term; otherwise the message is appended to r.pendingReadIndexMessages and no heartbeat is broadcast, so the request is held without any progress signal. releasePendingReadIndexMessages, invoked from the MsgAppResp handler when maybeCommit first advances the commit index, then feeds every queued message through sendMsgReadIndexResponse, which under the default ReadOnlySafe registers the request, records the leader's own acknowledgment and broadcasts a heartbeat carrying the rctx.
knowledge.conditions: StateLeader with the default ReadOnlySafe; the read request reaches the leader before its first commit in the current term; the leader stays leader and the commit that releases the queue is driven through the MsgAppResp path.

knowledge.statement: In the retained execution of the fixed experiment (three real raft instances for voters {1,2,3}, node 1 made leader with an uncommitted entry in term 1, default ReadOnlySafe, fault-free in-process delivery), a local MsgReadIndex submitted while committed_in_term was false left exactly one message in r.pendingReadIndexMessages, emitted no heartbeat and produced no read state (parsed index 0: committed 0, queued_after 1, heartbeats_emitted 0, read_states_after 0). After the replicated entry was delivered to the followers and their acknowledgments were stepped back, the leader's first commit in the term advanced committed to 1, committed_in_term became true, the queue drained to zero and the request was delivered as one read state carrying index 1 with no undelivered messages (parsed index 1: delivered true, queued_after 0, read_states_after 1, read_state_index 1). A subsequent local ReadIndex submitted after that commit was served through the usual ReadOnlySafe path with two heartbeats and two voter acknowledgments (parsed index 2: delivered true, read_states_added 1).

knowledge.statement: The confchange changer computes the resulting configuration and returns the error 'removed all voters' when the incoming voter set becomes empty (confchange/confchange.go:170-172), which the captured datadriven test treats as an expected changer-level rejection. The leader's propose-time validation does not compute the resulting voter set, so a proposal that removes the last voter passes (raft.go:1318-1335) and is appended like any other conf change; when the application later applies the committed entry, raft.applyConfChange converts the changer's error into a panic carrying that error text (raft.go:1961-1964, with the TODO to return the error to the caller), so the abort happens on the application's apply path rather than at proposal time.
knowledge.conditions: The proposal is a simple ConfChangeV2 (or ConfChange) that leaves no voter in the incoming configuration, made on a leader whose propose-time validation passes because no other conf change is pending and the configuration is not joint; the application then applies the committed entry through ApplyConfChange.

knowledge.statement: In the retained execution of the fixed experiment (single-voter cluster {1}, node 1 made leader in term 1 with committed 1 and applied 0, fault-free in-process), proposing a ConfChangeV2 that removes node 1 through MsgProp returned no error (parsed index 1: proposal_error '<nil>') and the entry was appended at index 2 and committed (committed true); applying that committed entry through the documented application path panicked with the verbatim recovered value 'removed all voters' and left the configuration unchanged (index 1: panicked true, recovered 'removed all voters', voters_after [1], node_state StateLeader). The control probe with an add-voter change of the same shape was accepted and committed the same way and applied without aborting (parsed index 3: panicked false, recovered empty, voters_after [1,2]).
knowledge.conditions: One executed in-process experiment with the fixed harness bytes of experiment e928fb3f495f4de9a5d56bef8b4c66e0-experiment (receipt 6c7f22d449564006a909a218643cfe08, exit 0, changed_target_files [], no parsing errors); a single-voter configuration, a direct becomeCandidate/becomeLeader setup, the proposal delivered as a MsgProp carrying an EntryConfChangeV2, and the application path modelled as a direct ApplyConfChange call with a recovering wrapper. One observed instance under these conditions, not a universal guarantee.

knowledge.statement: When a node applies a configuration in which it was a member before and is absent from the new voters (and from VotersOutgoing), node.run disables its proposal channel by setting propc to nil; Node.Propose/ProposeConfChange reach that channel through stepWithWaitOption, whose select can complete only on the channel send, on ctx.Done or on n.done. A proposal issued after such an application therefore blocks and returns only the caller's context error or ErrStopped, and the raft step path that would otherwise run (a follower forwarding the MsgProp to its leader) is never invoked, so the library's own drop signal (raft.go:1290-1295 for the removed-leader case) is not produced on this path.
knowledge.conditions: The node is driven through the Node API with an asynchronous run loop, it applied a committed configuration that removed it while it was in the previous configuration, its proposal channel was therefore disabled, and the caller supplies a context with a deadline (a non-expiring context blocks until the node stops).

knowledge.statement: In the retained execution of the fixed experiment (three-voter cluster {1,2,3}; node 1 a bare raft leader at term 1 with committed 1, node 2 a bare follower, node 3 driven through the Node API as a follower; fault-free in-process delivery; caller timeout 200 ms), Node.Propose on node 3 while it was still a member returned no error in 0 ms (parsed index 1: error_text '<nil>', elapsed_ms 0, blocked_until_deadline false, node3_in_config true). After a ConfChangeV2 removing node 3 was proposed on the leader and applied on node 3 through the Node API, node 3 was absent from the configuration with voters [1,2] (index 2: node3_in_config false, node3_lead 1, node3_state StateFollower, committed 3), and the same Node.Propose call then blocked for 201 ms and returned only the caller's context error (index 3: error_text 'context deadline exceeded', elapsed_ms 201, timeout_ms 200, blocked_until_deadline true).
knowledge.conditions: One executed in-process experiment with the fixed harness bytes of experiment b8fa9bc20e164089beff30308ce68220-experiment (receipt d5f37430774c4bbd9d64967e3f82290d, exit 0, changed_target_files [], no parsing errors); the subject node was driven through the Node API with its own Ready/Advance loop, the other voters were bare raft instances, the caller used a 200 ms context, and no restart, snapshot, leadership change or packet loss occurred. One observed instance under these conditions, not a universal guarantee.

knowledge.statement: In the retained execution of the successor experiment (three-voter cluster {1,2,3}; node 1 a bare raft leader at term 1 with committed 1, node 2 a bare follower, node 3 driven through the Node API as a follower; fault-free in-process delivery), Node.Propose on node 3 while it was a member returned no error in 0 ms (parsed index 1: error_text '<nil>', elapsed_ms 0, blocked_until_deadline false, node3_in_config true). After node 3 applied a ConfChangeV2 that removed it (index 2: node3_in_config false, voters [1,2], committed 3), a proposal with a 200 ms deadline blocked for the whole deadline and returned 'context deadline exceeded' (index 3: elapsed_ms 200, blocked_until_deadline true). A proposal issued with context.Background from a separate goroutine did not return during the fixed 300 ms observation window (index 4: returned_within_window false, error_text '<nil>', node3_in_config false), and it returned only after the node was stopped, with the error text 'raft: stopped' (index 5: returned_after_stop true).
knowledge.conditions: One executed in-process experiment with the fixed harness bytes of experiment 34e68e30368140d492185254dcedf04b-experiment (receipt 133c591601724c759fe07b2e80b55649, exit 0, changed_target_files [], no parsing errors); the subject node was driven through the Node API with its own Ready/Advance loop, the other voters were bare raft instances, the removal was proposed on the leader and applied on the subject node, no restart, snapshot or leadership change occurred, and the witness call was observed for 300 ms before the node was stopped. One observed instance under these conditions, not a universal guarantee.

knowledge.statement: In stepLeader, a MsgProp whose entry type is EntryConfChange or EntryConfChangeV2 is unmarshalled into the corresponding conf-change struct and any decode error panics the node processing the proposal (raft.go:1305-1313); nothing earlier on the path inspects the payload, because stepFollower relays a proposal by only rewriting m.To and sending it, without attaching a term or decoding the entries (raft.go:1714-1724 with raft.go:536-541). A proposal carrying an undecodable conf-change payload therefore aborts whichever node decodes it, and the follower that relays it neither rejects nor detects the problem.
knowledge.conditions: The receiver is a leader in the middle of handling MsgProp (for example a freshly elected leader in a three-voter configuration), the proposal is delivered either directly or through a follower that forwards proposals to its leader, and the entry type is a conf-change type with a payload that fails the library's protobuf decode.

knowledge.statement: In the retained execution of the fixed experiment (freshly elected three-voter clusters {1,2,3}, node 1 leader in term 1 with committed 1 and applied 1, fault-free in-process delivery), stepping a MsgProp carrying an EntryConfChangeV2 with the undecodable payload {0xff,0xff,0xff,0xff} directly into the leader panicked with the verbatim recovered value 'unexpected EOF' and left the last index unchanged at 1 (parsed index 1: leader_panicked true, last_index_before 1, last_index_after 1). Stepping the same proposal into follower 2 did not panic the follower, which forwarded exactly one MsgProp to node 1 (index 3: follower_panicked false, follower_messages 1, forwarded_to 1), and stepping that forwarded message into the leader panicked with the same recovered value 'unexpected EOF' while the last index stayed 1 (index 3: leader_panicked true). The control probe with a well-formed ConfChangeV2 of the same entry type was stepped into the leader without panicking and was appended (index 5: leader_panicked false, last_index_before 1, last_index_after 2).
knowledge.conditions: One executed in-process experiment with the fixed harness bytes of experiment 13bd8c6cd5cf4d318ed61aa3e6a05e6d-experiment (receipt 41c7e3db58b4436cb4f37208a4435f9c, exit 0, changed_target_files [], no parsing errors); the payloads were constructed by the harness, the proposals were stepped directly into the state machines, the relayed message was delivered by the harness, and no restart, snapshot, membership change or joint configuration was involved. One observed instance under these conditions, not a universal guarantee.

knowledge.statement: stepFollower handles MsgReadIndexResp by requiring exactly one entry: with any other count it logs an error naming the sender and the count and returns without recording anything, and only for a single-entry message does it append a ReadState carrying the message index and the entry data as the request context (raft.go:1766-1771). The read-index request direction has no comparable check: the leader's producer reaches Entries[0] through sendMsgReadIndexResponse and readOnly.addRequest (raft.go:1346-1363, 2142-2157, read_only.go:56-63).
knowledge.conditions: The receiver is a follower in the same term as the response's sender and reaches stepFollower's MsgReadIndexResp case; the message is delivered to the raft state machine directly.

knowledge.statement: In the retained execution of the fixed experiment (freshly elected three-voter cluster {1,2,3}, node 1 leader at term 1, node 2 the probed follower with lead 1, fault-free in-process delivery, read index 7 in every probe), a MsgReadIndexResp with zero entries was stepped into node 2 without panicking and added no read state (parsed index 1: panicked false, read_states_added 0, read_state_request_ctx ''), a MsgReadIndexResp with two entries likewise added no read state and did not panic (index 3: panicked false, read_states_added 0), and a MsgReadIndexResp with exactly one entry was accepted as one read state carrying index 7 and the request context 'assurance-rctx' (index 5: panicked false, read_states_added 1, read_state_index 7).
knowledge.conditions: One executed in-process experiment with the fixed harness bytes of experiment 252c693faf004ee5a79ecb81394a92ab-experiment (receipt 314e09224ab0436987767835f2a8d757, exit 0, changed_target_files [], no parsing errors); the responses were delivered directly to the raft state machine in the follower's own term, no request correlation was attempted, and no restart, snapshot, membership change or leadership change occurred. One observed instance under these conditions, not a universal guarantee.

knowledge.statement: In the retained execution of the varied-schedule experiment (freshly elected three-voter clusters {1,2,3}, node 1 leader, its own removal proposed, replicated, committed and applied on every node with the applied index advanced, fault-free delivery with the tick order rotated each round and the delivery order reversed on alternating rounds), the StepDownOnRemoval false probe kept node 1 as StateLeader outside the configuration and, across 120 varied rounds (parsed index 1), no eligible node took leadership (new_leader_elected false, new_leader_id 0, states_after_window {1: StateLeader, 2: StateFollower, 3: StateFollower}), the removal had committed (removal_committed true), last_index and committed_after stayed at 2, nothing was undelivered and the eligible voters' election timers were 1 and 0. With StepDownOnRemoval true the same varied window elected node 2 (index 3: new_leader_elected true, new_leader_id 2, states_after_window {1: StateFollower, 2: StateLeader, 3: StateFollower}).
knowledge.conditions: One executed in-process experiment with the fixed harness bytes of experiment 76e6ad3a9fa342638e9c16a1a27fdda6-experiment (receipt 118ff9bee5224b44a42aefba8d0ad788, exit 0, changed_target_files [], no parsing errors); every node was ticked once per round and every produced message was delivered, only the orders varied, and no restart, snapshot, partition, joint configuration or operator action was simulated. One observed instance under these conditions, not a universal guarantee.

knowledge.statement: The ReadOnlyLeaseBased option is validated at configuration time: Config.validate returns an error when it is selected without CheckQuorum (raft.go:334-335), and the option's documentation states that CheckQuorum MUST be enabled for it (raft.go:236-241). In the read path, the lease branch of sendMsgReadIndexResponse answers immediately by calling responseToReadIndexReq with the leader's committed index and sending the response to the requester without registering the request in readOnly or broadcasting a heartbeat (raft.go:2142-2157), while under ReadOnlySafe the same call registers the request, records the leader's own acknowledgment and broadcasts a heartbeat carrying the rctx. A lease-based follower also ignores MsgForgetLeader (raft.go:1745-1746), so the forget-leader mechanism that exists for the safe option is disabled in lease mode. Independently of the option, stepLeader defers a read request while the leader has not committed an entry in its current term (raft.go:1346-1363).
knowledge.conditions: The node is configured with ReadOnlyOption ReadOnlyLeaseBased and CheckQuorum enabled, is in StateLeader with a committed entry in its current term, and receives a local or forwarded MsgReadIndex; the follower-side statement applies to a node whose read-only option is lease-based receiving MsgForgetLeader.

knowledge.statement: A leader refuses a proposal that would push the uncommitted log tail over the configured size limit and reports it: increaseUncommittedSize returns false when the accumulated payload size would exceed MaxUncommittedEntriesSize while the uncommitted tail is non-empty (raft.go:2094-2111, and empty payloads are never refused), appendEntry logs a warning that the proposal is being dropped and returns false (raft.go:815-829), and the leader's MsgProp handler turns that into ErrProposalDropped for the caller (raft.go:1341-1343). By contrast, the conf-change validation branch in the same handler records its rejection only in an Infof line and substitutes an empty normal entry instead of returning an error.
knowledge.conditions: The node is StateLeader, the proposal is a MsgProp reaching stepLeader, the payload size is non-zero, and the current uncommitted payload size plus the new payload would exceed MaxUncommittedEntriesSize while the uncommitted tail is non-empty.

knowledge.statement: Node.Step returns nil for a message whose type is a local message type but whose From is not a local-message target, so an unexpected local message arriving from a remote peer is silently ignored with a code comment asking whether an error should be returned instead (node.go:478-483); every other message type is forwarded to the node's receive channel, and a MsgProp instead takes the proposal channel path whose completion set is the caller's context, the channel or the node's done channel. This is the same layer whose proposal call was observed to signal only the caller's deadline after the node applied its own removal.
knowledge.conditions: The node is driven through the Node API, the caller passes a message whose type is in the local-message set with a From that is not a local-message target, and the node is running so that Step reaches its local-message check.

This final turn is a source-grounded entry rather than a new execution, taken because the run's total budget expires at the end of this turn: it records the leader's periodic-heartbeat read-context behaviour with its sources - bcastHeartbeat attaches readOnly.lastPendingRequestCtx(), which is the rctx of the last entry in readIndexQueue or an empty value when the queue is empty (raft.go:722-730 with read_only.go:114-121), while each admission separately triggers bcastHeartbeatWithCtx with its own rctx through sendMsgReadIndexResponse and acknowledgments are tracked per context bytes by recvAck, with advance dequeuing statuses up to the acknowledged context (raft.go:2142-2157, read_only.go:68-112) - so a periodic heartbeat refreshes only the most recently admitted pending request, every pending request has already had its own admission-time broadcast, and no context is attached when nothing is pending. No investigation, interpretation or experiment is claimed, since the entry reports no observed instance; it exists because that distinction is what a reviewer needs when weighing the earlier coalescing and starvation findings, and the run can expire without any uninterpreted execution. The run's record stands as: nine answered questions with retained receipts and explicit counterevidence (rctx-coalescing starvation; its stale-index child; the deferred-read release that holds; the empty-Entries and undecodable-conf-change abort pair including the unvalidated follower relay; the silent conf-change replacement; the last-voter apply abort; the removed-leader stall with step-down control, external-trigger boundary and varied-schedule reproduction; and the Node API's deadline-only signal), the response-shape validation as a source-explained negative result, and four sourced Behaviour entries covering the proposal size-limit drop, the Node.Step local-message filter, the lease-read preconditions and this heartbeat-context mechanism - with no open necessary gaps and defect validity, CFT relevance and deduplication left to human offline review.

knowledge.statement: In StateLeader with the ReadOnlySafe option, when a MsgReadIndex arrives whose Entries[0].Data equals the rctx of a request that is already recorded in readOnly.pendingReadIndex, readOnly.addRequest returns early without storing the new request message, and sendMsgReadIndexResponse still attaches a heartbeat with that rctx (bcastHeartbeatWithCtx) and re-acknowledges the local node; the readIndexQueue and pendingReadIndex therefore keep exactly one status for the two admissions, and no second request message is retained.

knowledge.statement: On the acknowledging heartbeat, stepLeader asks readOnly.advance for the statuses up to the acknowledged ctx and then answers each returned status through responseToReadIndexReq(rs.req, rs.index): a status whose stored request came from a remote peer produces one MsgReadIndexResp addressed to that stored request's From, and a status whose stored request came from the leader itself appends one local ReadState. Only the request message of the first admission with a given rctx is stored, so admissions that were discarded by addRequest produce no read index answer of either kind.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlySafe with a quorum of heartbeat acknowledgments carrying the ctx, leader state unchanged between admission and acknowledgment, and the discarded admission having used the same rctx bytes as the stored one.

By contrast, the conf-change validation branch in the same handler records its rejection only in an Infof line and substitutes an empty normal entry instead of returning an error.

This is the same layer whose proposal call was observed to signal only the caller's deadline after the node applied its own removal.

knowledge.statement: The leader's periodic heartbeat path attaches the read-only context of only the most recently admitted pending request: bcastHeartbeat takes readOnly.lastPendingRequestCtx(), which returns the rctx of the last entry in readIndexQueue and an empty value when the queue is empty, and passes it to bcastHeartbeatWithCtx (raft.go:722-730 with read_only.go:114-121). Each admission instead triggers its own broadcast carrying that request's rctx through sendMsgReadIndexResponse, and acknowledgments are tracked per context bytes by readOnly.recvAck, with readOnly.advance dequeuing the statuses up to the acknowledged context (raft.go:2142-2157, read_only.go:68-112). So a periodic heartbeat refreshes only the latest pending request, every pending request has already had its own admission-time broadcast, and no context is attached when nothing is pending.
knowledge.conditions: The node is StateLeader with ReadOnlySafe; read requests are admitted through MsgReadIndex so that statuses exist in readOnly, and the heartbeat timer fires while the queue is either empty or non-empty.
